gaps.fact: New Zealand's position to the south east of Australia across the Tasman Sea, with the Court's distance of 4,100 km or 2,500 miles: no chapter, question or article places the country against Australia.

The Court files both Gisborne and Wairarapa as cool maritime. The Codex teaches Gisborne as warm and humid (the nz chapter, i-jtpu3q2u) and Martinborough as dry and windy, never under the words cool maritime, so a candidate meets a printed answer the Codex has not prepared. A chapter line should say both are maritime east coast regions in the Court's scheme, Gisborne the warmer.

The Court's Marlborough line, labelling requires 100% fruit from the region: only the marlborough article (law, labels, exam, traps and r-9c93kbgc) explains that the 100 per cent belongs to the private Appellation Marlborough Wine seal while the legal GI rule is 85 per cent; no chapter fact or Régionale or Village question asks it.

Gewürztraminer as a New Zealand white, and Riesling tied to Central Otago as the Court ties it: no chapter or bank question names either; Riesling is asked only for Waipara (i-zjfifc49), Gewürztraminer only by the gisborne article question r-9qpnup31.

Felton Road and Villa Maria are never the key to a Régionale or Village question: Felton Road is keyed only by the central-otago article question r-1jz6nns4 and the producers reference card, Villa Maria stands only as a wrong option in i-gv91mbr5 and r-falrjdmd and in three article producer lists (gisborne, hawkes-bay, marlborough).

The temperance movement and its long hold on New Zealand drinking (wine barred from restaurants until 1960 and supermarkets until 1990) is told only in the country overview; no chapter fact or question asks it.

The Scott Henry trellis: what it is (a divided canopy, the shoots of the upper canes trained upward and of the lower canes downward) is taught nowhere; the name appears only in the gisborne article and as a wrong option in i-9v77ldfy, and the training-pruning reading covers VSP alone.

How to open a screwcap at the table (present the bottle, grip the cap, break the seal by turning the bottle rather than the cap, then pour as usual): no SERVICE_REF table, chapter or question teaches it; the Codex covers screwcaps only as a closure (Wine Trade & Aging fact 6, c-x9ybck2f, c-cuckg1kr).

Sauvignon Blanc's ripe fruit set against sweet and savoury dishes such as mango salsa, and New Zealand Pinot Noir and Bordeaux blends offered as elegant non European options: no question or chapter fact frames a New Zealand wine in either role; only the general sugar and acid rules (i-ojddydgn, c-q7tsbnp9) stand in.

errors.where: js/data-questions.js, c-zovismb2: "ans": "The Geographical Indications (Wine and Spirits) Registration Act" and the explanation that opens with the same title; js/regions/new-zealand.json (country overview and law) and the New Zealand card in js/data-regions.js: "The Geographical Indications (Wine and Spirits) Registration Act 2006"
errors.claim: The statute that registers New Zealand's wine names is the Geographical Indications (Wine and Spirits) Registration Act.
errors.correction: Since 1 May 2024 the Act is titled the Geographical Indications Registration Act 2006 and covers other goods as well, after the European Union Free Trade Agreement Legislation Amendment Act 2024; the Geographical Indications Registration Regulations 2024 replaced the 2017 wine and spirits regulations. The accept list already takes the new title; the model answer and the explanation should give it, with the old title named as the one in force until 2024.
errors.source: Geographical Indications Registration Act 2006 as amended by the European Union Free Trade Agreement Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (legislation.govt.nz); Geographical Indications Registration Regulations 2024 (SL 2024/46).

courtUpdates.printed: Geographical Indications (GIs): trademark only with no minimums, no rules.
courtUpdates.now: From 1 May 2024 the GI statute was renamed the Geographical Indications Registration Act 2006 and widened beyond wine and spirits, under the New Zealand and European Union free trade agreement; new regulations of 2024 replaced those of 2017, and the European Union now protects the registered New Zealand wine and spirit GIs (23 by the reports found). No new wine GI registered since 8.2023 was found.
courtUpdates.source: Search: legislation.govt.nz, Geographical Indications Registration Regulations 2024 (SL 2024/46); Duncan Cotterill and Asia IP reports of the changes in force on 1 May 2024; IPONZ register pages (Bannockburn accepted September 2021).

notes: Mapped questions: Régionale 55 and Village 13 (New Zealand), 68 in all. Outside the mapped cats, i-gv91mbr5 (Producers & Icons, Cloudy Bay), i-le57zcor, i-iixuny58 and i-08oxahz2 (Geography & Maps), i-wiuy31pp and c-9oopzjj0 (Viticulture & Winemaking) meet Court rows, and the 51 article questions (r- ids) of the seven regional articles add Felton Road, Appellation Marlborough Wine, Gladstone and Gewürztraminer. The Régionale bank is unusually deep on the map and the chemistry: the Wairau and the Awatere, the Southern Valleys, Gimblett Gravels with its 1867 flood and soil boundary, Martinborough's 1970s survey and Tararua shelter, Gibbston and Bendigo, schist, frost, pyrazines and thiols, the screwcap's oxygen and the sustainability scheme. The Village bank adds thirteen good stems (the 95 per cent Gimblett Gravels licence, the GI nesting, UCD1, the 2001 initiative). The thin cells are Gewürztraminer, Felton Road and Villa Maria, Scott Henry, the screwcap service, the temperance years and the selling lines. Court text notes, never altered: its Introductory GI line (trademark only with no minimums) contradicts its own Wine Law row (85 per cent); it lists Gimblett Gravels among the GIs, though the name is a growers' trademark (the Codex teaches this rightly, r-or2ep5o6 and the country traps); its 4,100 km is far beyond the Tasman crossing (Sydney to Auckland is about 2,150 km), so any question should quote it as the Court's figure; its 100% Marlborough line belongs to the private seal. One error, medium: the GI Act's former title as the key of c-zovismb2. House rule note for the owner: the stem of i-nfdctcp4 keeps the American percent (seventy percent). Two searches spent: new GIs since 2023 (none found) and the 2024 change to the Act.
